The Patriots are coming off their bye week, which was much needed after their Week 10 loss against the Detroit Lions in Munich, where they lost Drake Maye to an ankle injury that could keep him out for the rest of the year. This means Tommy DeVito is set to start for the Pats against the Chargers, which gives Los Angeles a chance to pull out its second win of the season.

The Bolts entered this week as 1.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook. The over/under is currently set at 37.5 points.

The Chargers killed some of their momentum after beating the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, with a loss against the New York Jets. The Chargers trailed 17-3 with 3 minutes to go in the second quarter, forcing them to mount a comeback.

While Justin Herbert ran for a touchdown as time expired in the first half and completed two touchdowns to Ladd McConkey in the fourth quarter, they ultimately fell short by a field goal against the Jets.

Herbert entered the league’s concussion protocol following the game, and his status is up in the air for the contest against the Patriots.

content.value:
Week 11 ended in a less-than-ideal way for the Los Angeles Chargers in more ways than one.

Not only did the Chargers drop their Week 11 matchup to the New York Jets with a final score of 27-24; the team announced postgame that quarterback Justin Herbert will enter the concussion protocol.

Herbert was able to play for the entire game, going 15 of 21 for 131 yards, two touchdowns, no picks, and he took six sacks, which begins to explain the concussion. The Chargers were in this one right up until the end, but the Jets did just enough to snap their five-game losing streak and keep the Chargers from establishing a win streak for the first time this season.

The Chargers are technically not eliminated from postseason contention, but they are tied with the Dolphins and Titans for the worst record in the NFL at 1-9. And losing Herbert is unlikely to help.

DJ Uiagalelei is the next man up on the Chargers’ QB depth chart. The second-year signal caller signed with the Chargers as an undrafted free agent in 2025 after spending time at Clemson, Oregon State, and Florida State in college. He spent the 2025 season on the Chargers’ practice squad, and signed a futures contract with the team last offseason. He competed for the Chargers’ backup position behind Herbert with Trey Lance, but won the job when Lance landed on injured reserve in October. In 2026, he’s attempted seven passes, completing two, for 24 yards and a touchdown.

Trey Lance is currently on IR with a groin injury, but he is eligible to return at any point. There is no other quarterback on the Chargers’ active roster.

We will monitor this situation and update as more information becomes available.

content.value:
After backs spasms kept sidelined for the past two games, wide receiver Ladd McConkey returned to practice on Wednesday but participated in a limited fashion. He was one of five players who logged limited practices, joining cornerback Donte Jackson (groin), defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), offensive lineman Trey Pipkins (knee), and safety Kendall Williamson (calf).

The six remaining players on the injury report were all DNPs. Edge rusher Khalil Mack received his usual veteran’s rest day to begin the new week, but the other five players who worked off to the side were cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring), cornerback Rodney Shelley (ankle), tight end Charlie Kolar (concussion), and linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee).

Henley played 61 of 69 snaps against the Ravens on Monday night and Jim Harbaugh told reporters earlier Wednesday he would sit out practice with knee soreness.

Pipkins’ return could be something to watch should he be activated off of injured reserve this week. Harbaugh told reporters that rookie Logan Taylor would remain the starter after a standout performance against the Ravens. If right guard Cole Strange continues to underperform, there may be a chance Pipkins could relieve him of his duties. Kayode Awosika, who is now healthy, would also be a name to watch for that scenario, as well.

content.value:
The Los Angeles Chargers are getting ready for their Week 11 matchup against the New York Jets at SoFi Stadium.

While most of the players are getting ready, a few members of the team will be on the inactive list.

LB Daiyan Henley, CB Tarheeb Still, S Kendall Williamson, G Alex Harkey, WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith and WR Brenen Thompson are all out for the Chargers against the Jets.

  • Henley was already ruled out on the injury report, as he has been out of practice all week with a knee injury.
  • Thompson was doubtful, as he’s been dealing with a lingering hamstring injury.
  • Williamson was limited in practice at the beginning of the week but did not practice on Thursday or Friday, ruling him out for the contest.
  • Still was still questionable with an ankle injury, but he has also been ruled out.
  • Harkey and Lambert-Smith are healthy scratches.

Meanwhile, the inactives for the Jets are CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr., WR Omar Cooper Jr., WR Isaiah Williams, LB Trevin Wallace, TE Jelani Woods and EDGE Nate Lynn.

The Los Angeles Chargers are 1-8 going into their Week 11 matchup against the New York Jets at SoFi Stadium.

The Chargers can breathe a sigh of relief as they won’t go winless, but they have lost the inside path to the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

In this week’s Reacts poll, 43% of fans said they would be okay if the Chargers didn’t get the No. 1 overall pick.

The Chargers would have the chance to trade out of the pick with a team looking to select a quarterback, or they could take someone like Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, which could completely change their offense.

In last week’s Reacts poll, the confidence meter to determine whether the team is heading in the right direction, is at 13 percent.

It’s a slight step down from the 14 percent mark the team was at last week, but one win isn’t enough to rebuild all of the confidence zapped from the eight-game losing streak to start the season.

The Chargers are hoping to win their first home game of the year against the Jets at SoFi Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for Sunday at 1:05 pm PT. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

content.value:
The Chargers finally got their first win of the season by beating the Ravens on Monday Night Football who were forced to start quarterback Jacoby Brissett due to both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley being hurt. In Week 11, the Bolts could once again face a team without their starting quarterback if Geno Smith, who did not finish their most recent loss to the Bills, remains sidelined.

If that is the case, it would be backup Cade Klubnik manning the offense. Klubnik’s first ever NFL action came in Week 10, meaning the Chargers would have a much higher chance of winning their second consecutive game should he earn the start.

If Smith does end up pushing through and starting, then I’d start viewing this matchup as a toss-up. Smith has 12 touchdowns to just three picks this year as he’s gotten back to playing fairly good ball in his first season back with the Jets.

Defensively, the Jets are middle-of-the-pack. They rank 16th in total defense (332.1) and 22nd in scoring defense (25.4). The Chargers offense was better — at least on the ground — against the Ravens but the passing attacked remained underwhelming. Justin Herbert threw for just 38 yards on three completions in all of the final 30 minutes with only three players seeing more than two receptions, and only one of them was a wide receiver (Tre’ Harris).

With the Jets ranking fifth in pass defense this season, the Chargers’ game plan may end up being much of the same this week.

content.value:
The Chargers beat the Ravens to move to 1-8 on the season. The 0-17 jokes and hypotheticals can all finally stop.

Justin Herbert and the offense took a step forward with zero turnovers and a dominating performance on the ground with 160 yards, spurred by Omarion Hampton’s 105-yard night. Herbert also added 51 yards and a rushing score, as well.

Speaking of ground games, the Chargers held the Ravens to almost nothing on the ground. All-Pro back Derrick Henry was limited to just 10 yards on 10 carries. The zero yards on the ground for Baltimore during the first half was a historic low for the franchise.

You can’t be much more dominant than that.

Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Monday night.

Offense

Best

TE Charlie Kolar – 74.8
OG Logan Taylor – 74.4
QB Justin Herbert – 73.0
WR Tre’ Harris – 72.0
FB Scott Matlock – 70.2

It was poetic for Kolar — the former Baltimore Raven — to catch the first-down pass that helped seal the win over his former team. He was also dyamite in the run game, posting the second-high run block grade with a 74.6. His 76.4 pass block grade was also fourth best on the night.

Monday was Taylor’s best performance as a pro, finishing with zero pressures or sacks allowed on 27 dropbacks. His 81.1 pass block grade was tops on the team while his 68.9 in run blocking was fourth best.

For the first time all season, Herbert did not throw an interception and it led to his highest game grade of 2026.

Harris caught five passes for 86 yards all in the first half. Unfortunately he caught zero passes in the final 30 minutes of game time, but his yardage still gave him a new season and career high.

During the broadcast, it was shown that, at one point, the Chargers were averaging 5.1 yards per carry with Matlock on the field and 3.8 when he was not. He’s done an excellent job as the team’s starting fullback and I believe the switch from a zone-heavy run scheme to a gap scheme has benefitted both him and Hampton.

Worst

OT Travis Burke – 39.5
WR Quentin Johnston – 52.4
OG Cole Strange – 53.4
WR Derius Davis – 53.6
WR Theo Wease Jr. – 54.1

Unfortunately the team’s first win of the year was also one of Burke’s worst performances of the season. He allowed a team-high five pressures and had an abysmal 27.9 pass block grade to go with a penalty. The next worse grade among the offensive line was Strange with an above-average 64.0.

Johnston finished with one catch on one target for six yards. His season may be one of the biggest failures for Mike McDaniel in a season packed to the brim with them.

The aforementioned Strange allowed four pressures and was also called for a penalty. His 57.3 in run block was below average but still better than Joe Alt’s 53.2.

Defense

Best

LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 90.6
DT Teair Tart – 82.8
CB Donte Jackson – 77.4
EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu – 73.7
EDGE Khalil Mack – 73.0

What a night for Phillips, and also what a season it’s turning into for the first-year NFL starter. Phillips was a menace against the run on Monday night, helping the Chargers hold Derrick Henry to just 10 yards on 10 carries. He also snagged the team’s only interception off Jacoby Brissett when he sprinted under a deflected by Cam Hart. All night long, his high effort was apparent.

Tart had his highest-graded game of the season overall to go with his season-high 81.7 pass rush grade. He tied a season-high of three pressures, as well.

Jackson rebounded after a rough performance against the Texans to allow just one catch for six yards in three targets his way.

Mack and Tuli combined for 15 pressures on Brissett with the latter recording a nine by himself. His previous season high was six in Week Three.

Worst

S R.J. Mickens – 25.1
CB Deane Leonard – 28.5
S Elijah Molden – 40.9
LB Daiyan Henley – 51.7
DT Jamaree Caldwell – 53.9

Mickens luckily knocked down the Hail Mary attempt by the Ravens to seal the team’s first win of the season, but it was otherwise a bad night for the second-year safety. His overall game grade was his worst of the year by far and his 26.6 coverage grade was very much the same. Mickens was also called for his third penalty of the season.

Molden was credited with allowing five receptions on six targets towards him for 65 yards, including 53 after the catch. Henley also was dinged a bunch in coverage. PFF has him credited with a whopping nine receptions allowed on 11 targets in his area.
